overview: The commission reviewed several demolition and historic preservation matters, lifting a demolition delay for 130 Boston Avenue and determining Shiloh Baptist Church historically significant for CPA grant funding. It also scheduled a special October hearing for 16 Foster Court and voted down preferably preserved status for 80 Canal Street.

items.title: Preferably Preserved Hearing: 80 Canal Street
items.summary: The motion to find the property preferably preserved failed 0-5 after commissioners noted that past fire damage and alterations left little architectural integrity to preserve.

items.title: Demolition Delay Review: 130 Boston Avenue
items.summary: Approved lifting the demolition delay 5-0 following agreed-upon design revisions to rehabilitate the Queen Anne Victorian exterior.

items.title: Demolition Delay Review: 20 Otis Street
items.summary: Tabled the vote to lift the demolition delay to an upcoming special meeting to allow the applicant time to submit refined garage door options and trim details.

items.title: Determination of Significance: 11 Orchard Street
items.summary: A motion to find the Queen Anne two-family house significant failed 0-5, allowing the owner's renovation project to proceed.

items.title: Acceptance of Demolition Application: 8 Hamlin Avenue
items.summary: Accepted the demolition application and approved allocating $500 for a Form B historical survey.

items.title: Demolition Application and Hearing Schedule: 16 Foster Court
items.summary: Voted to accept the application under protest and scheduled a public hearing for October 3, 2022, also voting to add 20 Otis Street to that agenda.

items.title: Site Plan Reviews: 2-4 Capen Street and 50 Winthrop Street
items.summary: Commissioners agreed to review the proposed Tufts University designs and submit any comments to the chair by September 23 ahead of the October 5 deadline.

items.title: Historical Significance for CPA Application: Shiloh Baptist Church (1 Holton Street)
items.summary: Voted 5-0 to determine the church building historically significant to support its upcoming Community Preservation Act funding application.

items.title: General Updates and Old Business
items.summary: The commission reviewed ongoing surveys, Thomas Brooks Park artifact cataloging, and other administrative business before approving the August meeting minutes.
